title: Distinct Proteomic and Transcriptomic Profiles in T-cells and Monocytes in Patients with Common Variable Immunodeficiency.
projectDescription: A large subgroup of Common Variable Immunodeficiency (CVID) patients has autoimmune and inflammatory complications (CVIDCOMP), associated with T cell and monocyte pathology. This dataset comprises untargeted proteomic analyses of CD3+ T cells and CD14+ monocytes isolated from patients with CVID, CVIDCOMPCOMP, alongside with healthy controls.
sampleProcessingProtocol: The objective of the study was to identify differentially expressed proteins (DEPs) as well as differentially expressed mRNAS (DEGs)  that reflect the altered immune profiles characteristic of CVID normal compared to CVIDCOMP. Extended Methods will be available when published.
dataProcessingProtocol: Proteomic analyses were conducted on CD3+ T cells and CD14+ monocytes isolated from CVID patients and healthy controls. Protein pellets obtained via precipitation using the AllPrep DNA/RNA/Protein Mini Kit (Qiagen) were resuspended in 8M urea, 30 mM Tris pH 8.0, 4 % CHAPS containing 5 mM Tris(2-carboxyethyl)phosphine (TCEP). 25 µg protein of each sample was transferred to a 96-deep well plate and incubated with 1% sodium deoxycholate (SDC), 100 mM Tris-HCl pH8.5, 10 mM TCEP and 40 mM Chloroacetamide (CAA) for simultaneous reduction and alkylation. On beads trypsin digestion was performed in the King Fisher automated system using HILIC microspheres (Resyn Biosciences), according to manufacturer’s instructions. Briefly, the protein lysates were diluted in binding buffer (0.5 % SDS, 30 % Acetonitrile, 200 mM NH4Ac pH 4.5) and incubated with 400 ug of HILIC microspheres previously equilibrated in 15% Acetonitrile, 100 mM NH4Ac pH 4.5. After two washes in 95 % acetonitrile, on-beads digestion was performed with Trypsin (1 mg/well) in 15 mM NH4HCO2 pH 8.2. Peptides were dried out in a Speed Vac, reconstituted in 0.1 % Formic acid and centrifuged at maximum speed at 4 oC. The supernatants, containing peptides, were transferred to HPLC vials. Peptides were analyzed via LC-MS/MS on a timsTOF Pro 2 (Bruker Daltonics) connected to a nanoElute (Bruker Daltonics) HPLC, as previously described in https://doi.org/10.1016/j.mtbio.2025.101474. Database  search for protein identification was performed via MaxQuant (https://www.nature.com/articles/nbt.1511) using the Human reference proteome including isoforms and unreviewed proteins (https://www.uniprot.org/), as described in https://doi.org/10.1016/j.mtbio.2025.101474.
